label: Headless mode is -p/--prompt: prompt from the flag argument, from stdin when the flag carries no value, or from --prompt-file; --workdir sets the working directory and --output selects text, json or streaming.
Four headless-only limits exist: --max-turns, --max-price (cumulative across root session and subagents), --max-tokens, and --time-limit, which writes the export and exits 3.

Dispatch knobs cover agent profile (--agent with builtin ask, accept-edits, smart-approve, auto-approve or a ~/.vibe/agents TOML), model alias, approvals (--auto-approve/--yolo, --smart-approve), tool allow/deny lists, trust, extra dirs, worktree and system prompt file.

Exit codes are closed: 0 finished, 1 usage or config error, 2 infrastructure failure, 3 limit or refusal (turn, token, price, deadline, terminated, length, refusal), 4 aborted by the agent-socket server.
--output-dir writes export.json on every exit with version, effective config, token usage, cost, stop reason and outcome, plus the session journal and each subagent journal.
An unauthenticated live dispatch exits 1, leaves stdout empty, prints a keychain notice and 'Error: Missing MISTRAL_API_KEY environment variable for mistral provider' on stderr.
The vibe console script execs a bundled 28 MB Rust binary, so headless rendering is Rust-side; the Python package supplies the app server and ACP engines.

The protocol launch surface AgentConfig carries headless, workdir, agent, auto_approve, enabled and disabled tools, max_turns, max_price, max_session_tokens, trust_workspace, system_prompt, mcp_servers, client tools and client hooks.
